autocomplete_and_input_purpose_note: Contact fields keep useful autocomplete and input-purpose cues so browsers and assistive technology can help rather than guess.
contact_method_scope_note: Each critical route says whether it needs a phone number, an email address, or either one, and whether a bounded alternate method or help path exists.
contact_target_verification_surface_labe: Example State official voter-information contact-target and verification-code fail-open policy
delivery_failure_recovery_note: The route distinguishes malformed contact data, unsupported channel type, delivery failure, expired code, mismatch, and temporary throttle states, while keeping a first-party help lane visible.
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes that depend on a phone number, email address, or verification code keep channel requirements, ordinary entry posture, code-entry behavior, and bounded recovery clear enough that the current official answer does not depend on guessing which delivery target works.
no_surprise_auto_submit_note: Completing a contact field or code does not silently change context or submit the route without a clear, predictable cue.
ordinary_entry_note: Phone numbers and email addresses allow ordinary typed and pasted entry without unnecessary re-entry or brittle local parsing.
same_answer_across_contact_method_varian: Equivalent email- and SMS-based routes resolve to the same authoritative answer or the same bounded recovery posture when the jurisdiction offers both.
sms_and_region_requirement_note: The route states before failure whether a U.S. number or an SMS-capable mobile number is required for code delivery.
verification_code_entry_note: Verification-code fields support paste, accessible review, and predictable correction without making segmented code boxes the only workable posture.
